events.title: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 earnings (AI semis test)
events.why_it_matters: After Nvidia's $96.2B quarter and Dell's AI-server beat, Broadcom is the next confirmation of custom AI silicon and networking demand.
events.what_to_watch: AI semiconductor revenue vs ~$16B guide, Q4/FY26 AI trajectory vs $56B, and any margin compression from custom-chip mix.

events.title: Snowflake Q2 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Enterprise data/AI software bellwether reports after the close alongside Broadcom and HPE, testing whether AI spend is still broadening beyond hardware.
events.what_to_watch: Product revenue vs ~$1.48–1.51B, net revenue retention, RPO, and AI-product commentary.

events.title: HPE Q3 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Networking/AI server peer to Dell; a beat would corroborate the infrastructure supercycle beyond Nvidia/Dell.
events.what_to_watch: Networking/AI segment growth, revenue vs ~$11.5–12.1B, EPS vs ~$0.92, and FY guidance.

events.title: ADP August private payrolls
events.why_it_matters: Last private-payroll pulse before Friday's NFP; July was a weak +44k, and a similar print would keep the labor-slowdown case alive into Warsh's FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~+47k vs July +44k; a large miss would cut September hike odds, a large beat would reinforce them.

events.title: Costco August monthly sales
events.why_it_matters: High-frequency read on US consumer resilience into a possible Fed hike and Canada tariff shock.
events.what_to_watch: Comparable sales ex-gas/FX vs July's +8.9% comps / +10.7% net sales; any traffic vs ticket split.

events.title: US–Iran strikes reopen Hormuz oil shock
events.why_it_matters: Fresh US airstrikes and Iranian retaliation have pushed Brent back above ~$95 (WTI ~$91), reopening the energy-inflation channel that already lifted ECB hike odds and Warsh's hawkish case.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Hormuz flows stay restricted vs de-escalation; a return toward the earlier ~$120 spike would be regime-like for rates and risk assets.

events.title: FOMC September decision (first Warsh SEP/dots)
events.why_it_matters: Funds rate is 3.50–3.75%; Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech has lifted 25bp hike odds to ~59–68%, making this the cycle's highest-stakes meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Friday NFP and Sep 11 CPI as the last two gates; a hold vs 25bp hike, the new SEP, and any dissent.

events.title: US August employment report (NFP)
events.why_it_matters: July payrolls fell 23k (first negative print of the cycle) even as unemployment eased to 4.1%; August is the last jobs print before the Warsh FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~+55–58k, unemployment unchanged at 4.1%, AHE ~+0.2–0.3% m/m; a second negative print would undercut a hike.

events.title: US August CPI
events.why_it_matters: July CPI was +0.1% m/m / +3.4% y/y (core +0.2% / +2.5%); Warsh called inflation 'concerning' with PCE still near 3.7%, so a hot August print would all but lock a September hike.
events.what_to_watch: Early street sketches (e.g. TD) point to a firmer ~+0.4% headline / ~+0.24% core as gasoline and shelter rebound; consensus still coalescing.

events.title: US August PPI
events.why_it_matters: Producer prices the day before CPI will show whether energy, tariffs, and AI-capex goods inflation are still feeding into consumer prices.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs July unchanged m/m / +4.7% y/y; pipeline energy and capital-goods components.

events.title: ECB rate decision (Berlin)
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate is 2.25%; euro-area flash CPI jumped to 3.3% y/y in August on energy, and markets price ~85–95% odds of a 25bp hike to 2.50%.
events.what_to_watch: 25bp hike vs hold, Lagarde's energy/second-round language, and whether this is a one-and-done or a new tightening leg.

events.title: ISM Services PMI (August)
events.why_it_matters: Services are the bulk of the US economy; July was 54.1, so another expansion print would sit awkwardly next to a possible hike and a weak goods-jobs pulse.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs July 54.1, prices-paid, and employment sub-index ahead of Friday NFP.

events.title: Initial jobless claims (pre-NFP)
events.why_it_matters: Last high-frequency labor print before Friday's payrolls; claims near ~205k would keep the 'soft but not breaking' narrative intact.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~205k for the week ending Aug 29; a sharp rise would amplify July's -23k NFP shock.

events.title: Fed Governor Waller economic-outlook interview
events.why_it_matters: Waller has been the public counterweight to Warsh's hike tilt; this is likely the last notable Fed speak before blackout.
events.what_to_watch: Whether he still leans hold/cut versus endorsing Warsh's 'we have work to do' inflation line.

events.title: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' iPhone 18 event
events.why_it_matters: First hardware event under CEO John Ternus; expected iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and a rumored first foldable, with base iPhone 18 reportedly slipped to spring 2027.
events.what_to_watch: Foldable pricing/availability, China channel commentary, and whether AI-on-device is more than a slogan.

events.title: Canada dollar-for-dollar tariffs take effect
events.why_it_matters: After talks collapsed Aug 21, Ottawa matches US 50% tariffs on ~$20–28B of US goods (steel, furniture, apparel, dairy, electronics) from 12:01 a.m. EDT Sep 8.
events.what_to_watch: Any last-minute pause, auto/USMCA leakage, and pass-through into US PPI/CPI.

events.title: Section 232 drone/UAS tariffs effective
events.why_it_matters: Proclamation of Aug 13 imposes 100% duties on larger/thermal UAS and 25% on smaller drones from 12:01 a.m. ET Sep 3, aimed at China supply chains with allied 10–15% caps.
events.what_to_watch: CBP HTS guidance, Blue UAS exemptions delayed to Feb 2027, and any China retaliation in components.

events.title: Adobe Q3 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Software/AI-monetization test the same week as CPI and the ECB; a miss would undercut the 'AI everywhere' bid outside semiconductors.
events.what_to_watch: Net-new ARR, Firefly/GenAI attach, and FY guide after the close Sep 10.

events.title: Oracle Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: OCI/AI cloud backlog is one of the few mega-cap checks on whether hyperscaler capex is still converting into contracted revenue before the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Cloud infrastructure growth, RPO, and capacity-ramp commentary; calendars cluster around Sep 14 after close.

events.title: OPEC+ eight-country review (post-188kbd hike)
events.why_it_matters: The Aug 2 deal lifts September quotas by 188kbd, completing the 1.65M bpd voluntary-cut unwind, but actual barrels are constrained by Iran/Hormuz disruptions.
events.what_to_watch: A widely expected pause in further hikes versus any emergency response to the oil spike.

events.title: US existing-home sales (August)
events.why_it_matters: Housing is the rate-sensitive sector most exposed if Warsh hikes into already-high mortgage costs.
events.what_to_watch: NAR August existing-home sales at 10:00 a.m. ET Sep 10, same morning as PPI.

events.title: US August retail sales
events.why_it_matters: Drops the same morning as the FOMC decision, so a strong or weak consumer print can immediately reprice the hike.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales vs gasoline-distorted headline; Census release 8:30 a.m. ET Sep 16.

events.title: Nvidia Q2 FY2027 blowout (still in play)
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), data center $89.0B, net income $59.7B, Q3 guide $108B ±2% — still the market's core bull case.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Broadcom tonight and Oracle on Sep 14 validate the $108B guide rather than fade it.

events.title: Dell Q2 FY2027 AI-server beat and raise
events.why_it_matters: Revenue $47.0B vs ~$44.9B, adj. EPS $7.04 vs ~$4.92, AI servers $16.4B, backlog $95B; FY revenue raised to $192B and AI-server sales to $74B.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through in Broadcom/HPE tonight and whether input-cost/price hikes leak into PPI.

events.title: JOLTS job openings (July)
events.why_it_matters: Openings were little changed at 7.27M (4.4% rate) after a sharp downward revision to June, consistent with a low-churn, cooling labor market.
events.what_to_watch: Friday NFP to confirm whether payrolls rebound from July's -23k.

events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August)
events.why_it_matters: PMI cooled to 54.6 from 55.6 (consensus ~55.2) but stayed in expansion for an eighth month, with prices still extremely hot at 71.1.
events.what_to_watch: Whether sticky ISM prices plus oil feed August CPI; services PMI tomorrow.

events.title: China official manufacturing PMI (August)
events.why_it_matters: Official PMI rose to 49.8 from 49.2 but remains in contraction; Caixin/private gauge was 51.5 — still no broad PBoC easing in early September.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Beijing adds targeted easing if the sub-50 streak continues; export-order bounce vs weak domestic demand.

events.title: South Korea August chip-export boom
events.why_it_matters: Semiconductor exports hit a record $46.65B (+209% y/y), lifting total exports 68.7% — hard confirmation of the AI memory/server cycle outside US earnings.
events.what_to_watch: Sustainability into Q4 and any US memory-equipment controls biting Chinese fabs.

events.title: Eurozone August HICP flash (3.3%)
events.why_it_matters: Headline inflation jumped to 3.3% (highest since 2023) on energy +14.3% y/y, cementing September ECB hike bets even as core eased to 2.4%.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 10 ECB decision and Sep 17 final HICP; energy pass-through if Hormuz stays disrupted.

events.title: Warsh Jackson Hole speech (hawkish reset)
events.why_it_matters: Chair Warsh said inflation remains too high (PCE ~3.7%) and 'we have work to do' unless underlying inflation is clearly returning to 2%, lifting September hike odds from ~35% to a coin-flip-plus.
events.what_to_watch: Whether NFP/CPI give him cover to follow through on Sep 16.

events.title: SHEIN Hong Kong IPO debut
events.why_it_matters: Priced at HK$48.56, raising ~US$1.7B at ~US$26.5B value (vs ~$100B 2022 peak); shares slid as much as ~10% on debut amid growth, de minimis, and forced-labor overhangs.
events.what_to_watch: Aftermarket into the 6-month lockup (March 2027); no other mega IPOs in this window.

events.title: John Ternus becomes Apple CEO
events.why_it_matters: Tim Cook's succession took effect Sep 1; hardware-engineer Ternus now owns the product cycle, China risk, and on-device AI into next week's event.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 9 keynote tone on China, foldable, and AI.

events.title: House passes FY2027 CR through Dec 11
events.why_it_matters: House cleared the Senate CR (H.R. 6500) 370–48, funding government through Dec 11 at FY2026 levels and taking October shutdown risk off the table pending Trump's signature.
events.what_to_watch: Presidential signature in the next day or two; full-year bills slip to a lame-duck after the midterms.

events.title: EO 14420: national emergency on U.S. bulk-power system
events.why_it_matters: IEEPA emergency lets DOE block/condition foreign-produced grid equipment (transformers, inverters, BESS, industrial controls) from covered foreign entities, with implementing rules due within 120 days.
events.what_to_watch: Covered-foreign-entity list, pre-qualified vendor roster, and whether China-origin T&D/inverter/BESS supply is restricted into AI-data-center interconnection queues.

events.title: OFAC Operation Economic Outcast / EO 13902 Iran sector determinations
events.why_it_matters: Treasury opened secondary-sanctions risk on Iran digital assets, technology, gold, aviation, and shipping, designated ~60 parties/vessels, and suspended Iran-related general licenses—distinct from the kinetic Hormuz shock.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-on SDN hits on third-country shippers/banks, gold and crypto rails, and any freight/insurance premia on Hormuz-adjacent trade.

events.title: Beef TRQ expansion: +300k mt lean trimmings
events.why_it_matters: Proclamation adds 300,000 mt of in-quota lean beef trimmings in three 100k-mt tranches (first opened Sep 1) to cap ground-beef prices after the U.S. herd hit a 75-year low.
events.what_to_watch: Whether imported trimmings clear at the 25% discount trigger; if not, the White House can cancel remaining quota.

events.title: SEC proposes Regulation Crypto Assets
events.why_it_matters: FR publication of a tailored offering regime (startup/$5M and fundraising/$75M exemptions plus an investment-contract safe harbor) is the first comprehensive SEC crypto capital-formation proposal of the cycle.
events.what_to_watch: Comment-file intensity through Oct 20 and whether exchanges/issuers treat the safe harbor as a de-securities path.

events.title: UMich August final sentiment 51.7; 1y inflation 4.0%
events.why_it_matters: Final sentiment fell to 51.7 from 55.2 as gasoline/Iran inflation fears dominated; year-ahead inflation expectations eased only to 4.0% (from 4.2%), still hot versus Warsh's hike case.
events.what_to_watch: September preliminary (Sep 11, same morning as CPI) for whether energy shock is still lifting household inflation expectations.

events.title: China official non-manufacturing PMI stays at 49.0
events.why_it_matters: Primary logged only the manufacturing 49.8 print; official non-manufacturing stayed in contraction at 49.0, underscoring weak domestic services demand and no early-September PBoC/NDRC impulse.
events.what_to_watch: Whether NDRC accelerates already-budgeted consumer subsidies or waits for the mid-September LPR window (outside this scan).

events.title: Eurozone manufacturing PMI 52.7 (4-year high)
events.why_it_matters: Factory PMI jumped to 52.7 from 51.9 with the strongest new orders since 2022, reinforcing the ECB's ~85–95% hike path alongside the 3.3% HICP flash the primary already has.
events.what_to_watch: Sep 10 ECB statement for whether Lagarde treats the PMI rebound as demand-driven or energy-price pass-through.

events.title: Palo Alto Networks Q4 FY2026 beat
events.why_it_matters: Cybersecurity platform bellwether printed $3.41B revenue (+34% y/y) and $1.02 adj. EPS, with NGS ARR +63% to $9.10B—the main non-semis software check the primary skipped.
events.what_to_watch: FY27 guide ($14.10–$14.20B) conversion vs. multiple compression if shares fade the beat.

events.title: EIA weekly crude inventories (week of Aug 28)
events.why_it_matters: First official U.S. stock print after the latest Hormuz flare; prior week showed commercial crude +0.1mb to 428.9mb while SPR fell 3.7mb to 289.7mb, and API flagged a 2.6mb commercial draw.
events.what_to_watch: Commercial crude vs. SPR split and product yields; a large commercial build would undercut the $95 Brent spike, a draw would validate it.

events.title: U.S. 10-year and 30-year Treasury reopenings
events.why_it_matters: Off-quarter reopenings (~$39B 10s on Sep 9, ~$22B 30s on Sep 10) land into Warsh hike odds of ~59–68% and will set term-premium into the Sep 15–16 FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Tail ratios, indirect/foreign take-up, and whether buyback ops cap the long end.

events.title: Empire State manufacturing survey (September)
events.why_it_matters: Drops 8:30 a.m. ET on FOMC day 1, so a hot prices-paid or employment print can immediately color Warsh's first SEP/dots.
events.what_to_watch: Prices-paid vs. new-orders split relative to ISM manufacturing's still-hot 71.1 prices index.

events.title: UK August CPI (ONS)
events.why_it_matters: July CPI was already 2.9% y/y; the August print lands the same morning as the FOMC decision and will reprice BoE Sep 17 hike risk after energy's rebound.
events.what_to_watch: Core/services vs. energy contribution; a 3-handle would lift GBP and global rate-hike correlation into Warsh.

top_risks: Hot August CPI plus a firm NFP locking a Warsh 25bp hike on Sep 16 into already-elevated real yields
US–Iran/Hormuz escalation driving oil from ~$95 back toward the earlier ~$120 spike and imported inflation in the US and euro area
Canada's matching tariffs on ~$20–28B of US goods from Sep 8, stacking on drone 232 duties from Sep 3
Synchronized hawkish reset: ECB ~85–95% priced to hike Sep 10 while the Fed is a live hike call
Broadcom (and HPE/Snowflake) failing to confirm Nvidia/Dell, which would puncture the only durable equity offset
top_opportunities: Dell's $95B AI-server backlog and $192B FY raise already validate Nvidia; a Broadcom beat tonight extends the capex bid
A weak NFP/claims sequence that forces Warsh to hold, relieving duration and high-beta tech
Korea's record $46.7B chip exports as independent confirmation of the memory/AI hardware cycle
CR passage removing the October shutdown tail risk into midterms
Apple foldable/iPhone 18 Pro event as a consumer-tech product-cycle catalyst if pricing is not prohibitive
summary: September 2 is an AI-earnings and oil day: Broadcom/HPE/Snowflake report after the close while a fresh US–Iran flare has Brent back above $95 rather than the $120 spike of earlier in the war. The policy path is still binary — Warsh hike odds ~59–68% into Sep 15–16, gated by Friday's NFP (~+55–58k after July's -23k) and Sep 11 CPI — and the ECB is now an ~85–95% hike on Sep 10 after euro-area inflation hit 3.3%. Offsets are Dell's blowout, Korea's chip-export boom, and a House-passed CR that largely kills the October shutdown risk; Canada's tariffs still hit Sep 8.

catcher.coverage_assessment: Primary was strong on mega-cap AI earnings, the Warsh/FOMC data path, Hormuz oil, and the three trade/funding items it did catch (House CR, Canada tariffs, Section 232 drones). It was nearly blind to executive orders, OFAC sectoral sanctions, SEC crypto rulemaking, and the entire second-tier macro/FI stack (UMich, China services PMI, EZ factory PMI, auctions, EIA, Empire State, UK CPI).
catcher.biggest_gap: EO 14420 (Aug 26) declaring a national emergency to restrict foreign-produced bulk-power equipment—highest-impact government action in-window, with direct read-through to utilities, grid OEMs, and AI power-infrastructure supply chains.
